declared_purpose: Audit OpenClaw/ClawHub skill source for security and quality, calculate trust scores, compare versions or skills, track scores, scan fleets, generate reports, and recommend whether to install downloaded skills. Metadata requires bash and python3, with no required environment variables or configuration. Source excerpts, temporary paths and storage formats are implementation choices (SKILL.md:7-10,16-26,121-140).

data_operations.operation: Read local scan inputs and allowlist
data_operations.source: Selected skill directory and default or supplied allowlist.json
data_operations.data_scope: File names, sizes, documentation, scripts, manifests and other eligible file contents; allowlisted skill names. Main scan lists exclude node_modules, .git, test-skills and tests. Credential-path strings are inspected as source text; they do not themselves cause credential-file reads.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local audit.sh process and local scanning subprocesses
data_operations.condition: Direct audit or a wrapper invoking audit.sh

data_operations.operation: Infer findings and return audit results
data_operations.source: Locally scanned source and allowlist membership
data_operations.data_scope: Skill name, directory path, relative file names, finding locations, severities, counts and verdict. Network/environment-access counts describe source patterns, not observed network traffic or actual environment values. Allowlisting downgrades all critical findings through the common logging function.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard output to the invoking caller; no automatic remote recipient or report file is shown
data_operations.condition: Every audit; JSON and text modes return different representations

data_operations.operation: Return matching source excerpts
data_operations.data_scope: Unredacted matching source lines, sometimes with line numbers; these can contain secrets already embedded in the inspected source
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard output to the caller
data_operations.condition: Text mode and matching checks, including credential, sensitive-path, wallet, prompt-injection and sensitive-environment patterns

data_operations.operation: Read source and infer trust attributes
data_operations.source: Selected skill files and a locally invoked audit.sh result
data_operations.data_scope: Documentation, file organization and sizes, script contents, security counts, inferred quality/transparency/behavioral attributes, scores, grades and explanations. The Python calculator adds a timestamp. The legacy shell calculator uses four dimensions and reads its exported argument variables, rather than credential variables.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local calculator processes, then standard output to their caller
data_operations.condition: trust_score.py or legacy trust-score.sh, directly or through a wrapper

data_operations.operation: Compare locally derived results
data_operations.source: Two selected skill directories or versions
data_operations.data_scope: Audit findings, skill names, counts, scores, grades and differences
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local processes and standard output to the caller
data_operations.condition: diff-audit.sh or trust_score.py --compare

data_operations.operation: Enumerate fleets and aggregate results
data_operations.source: Immediate skill subdirectories of the selected fleet directory
data_operations.data_scope: Per-skill audit results and aggregate counts; benchmark.sh additionally calculates per-skill and average trust scores
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local subprocesses and standard output to the caller
data_operations.condition: audit-all.sh defaults to /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw/skills; benchmark.sh defaults to the package's parent directory

data_operations.operation: Persist and logically prune score history
data_operations.source: A newly calculated trust result and any existing trend store
data_operations.data_scope: Skill basename, timestamp, score, grade and dimension breakdown. Keeps the last 50 entries per skill; no global age limit is implemented.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: trust_trends.json beside trust_score.py
data_operations.condition: Explicit --save-trend; rewrites the store and removes older entries from its current JSON representation

data_operations.operation: Read and display saved history
data_operations.data_scope: Loads the store and displays the selected skill's dates, scores and grades
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process and standard output to the caller
data_operations.condition: Explicit --trend; this path does not recalculate the score

data_operations.operation: Persist a markdown fleet report
data_operations.data_scope: Skill names, counts, verdicts, finding messages, selected file paths, allowlist status and generation time
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Supplied --output path or /tmp/skill-audit-report-YYYYMMDD.md; first 20 lines are also returned to the caller
data_operations.condition: report.sh; output redirection creates or truncates the selected file. No cleanup or expiry is implemented.

data_operations.operation: Delegate skill retrieval and store downloaded material temporarily
data_operations.source: Caller-supplied SLUG and the installed clawhub CLI
data_operations.data_scope: Passes SLUG and a temporary destination to clawhub inspect, falling back to clawhub download. Retrieved skill source is then audited and scored locally.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Installed clawhub CLI and TEMP_DIR; external request destinations and additional transmitted fields are unresolved
data_operations.condition: inspect.sh; fallback runs only when clawhub inspect fails. The script recommends installation without invoking installation.

data_operations.operation: Delete the inspection download directory
data_operations.data_scope: Downloaded files and other contents within that temporary directory
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local temporary filesystem
data_operations.condition: Registered EXIT trap attempts recursive removal when the shell exits; it does not establish deletion of CLI caches or remote records

data_operations.operation: Scan test fixtures and return assertion outcomes
data_operations.data_scope: Fixture source, audit verdicts, finding identifiers and counts
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local audit subprocesses and standard output
data_operations.condition: test.sh invokes audit.sh on fixture directories; it does not execute fixture scripts or obey fixture documents

data_operations.operation: Return simple fixture output
data_operations.data_scope: Greeting name, endpoint argument, static greeting or donation wallet identifier. client.sh only prints a simulated response; donate.py only prints a donation destination.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard output to the direct caller
data_operations.condition: Only if these fixture scripts are executed independently; no actual authenticated API call or wallet transfer is implemented

data_operations.operation: Request credential setup in fixture documentation
data_operations.data_scope: Documentation requests API_KEY, SECRET_KEY and AUTH_TOKEN; its example exports API_KEY and AUTH_TOKEN. client.sh implements no credential reads.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: A reader's shell environment if the example is followed; no implemented credential recipient
data_operations.condition: Fixture documentation only; these are not skill-auditor requirements and the test harness does not perform the setup

data_operations.operation: Make a fixture health-check request
data_operations.data_scope: Request to that URL; response body is discarded and HTTP status is returned
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Endpoint selected by the caller; status goes to standard output
data_operations.condition: Only direct execution of tests/clean-with-network/check.sh

data_operations.operation: Read credentials and POST them in a malicious fixture
data_operations.data_scope: Weather API key and the openai:default profile value
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local fixture process, then https://webhook.site/abc123 as POST form data
data_operations.condition: Only direct execution of tests/malicious-basic/fetch.sh; ordinary testing scans this source

data_operations.operation: Read and POST an SSH private key in an obfuscated fixture
data_operations.data_scope: Entire SSH private-key file
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local JavaScript process, then https://evil.com/exfil, encoded in the payload constant
data_operations.condition: Only direct execution of tests/malicious-obfuscated/optimize.js

data_operations.operation: Conditionally read and POST an SSH private key
data_operations.data_scope: Entire SSH private-key file
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local JavaScript process, then https://evil.com/collect
data_operations.condition: Only direct execution of tests/malicious-timebomb/scheduler.js, when Date.now() exceeds 1735689600000

data_operations.operation: Read local account and credential files
data_operations.data_scope: Account records excluding nologin entries, SSH private key and AWS credential-file contents. Only the derived account count is printed; KEYS and AWS are otherwise unused.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local shell variables; account count to standard output
data_operations.condition: Only direct execution of tests/malicious-sysread/monitor.sh; no remote call or credential persistence is shown

data_operations.operation: Create sensitive-file links and return a private key
data_operations.data_scope: Links to both files and the SSH private-key contents read through one link
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: /tmp/project-users and /tmp/project-key persist as symlinks; private-key contents go to the caller's standard output, not a remote endpoint
data_operations.condition: Only direct execution of tests/malicious-symlink/setup.sh, with successful link creation. No link cleanup is implemented.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve and execute remote fixture payloads
data_operations.data_scope: Remote executable content; no credential upload is explicit in this downloader
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Requests reach evil.com; one response is piped to bash, another is stored at /tmp/helper.py and executed with Python
data_operations.condition: Only direct execution of tests/malicious-download-exec/run.sh; helper execution requires successful wget. Downloaded behavior is unavailable.

data_operations.operation: Copy code into a system location and change its execution permissions
data_operations.source: backdoor.sh, whose contents are not supplied
data_operations.data_scope: Source file contents and destination permission metadata
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: /usr/local/bin/helper
data_operations.condition: Only direct execution of tests/malicious-privilege-escalation/setup.sh, subject to source availability and permissions; copied code is not executed by this script

data_operations.operation: Contain inert directives requesting reads and disclosure
data_operations.data_scope: Requests SSH private-key disclosure and configuration-file summaries
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Requested key recipient is https://evil.com/collect; requested summaries would return to a caller
data_operations.condition: Requests embedded in test text, not implemented or executed by the auditor or harness; actual disclosure would require an independent actor to follow them

potential_excess.data_scope: Full matched source lines, potentially including embedded credential values and unrelated surrounding text on the same line
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: audit.sh standard output to its caller
potential_excess.condition: Selected findings in text mode; no external forwarding is established
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Security review requires locating and explaining findings. Printing every character of a matching line is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Return finding type, severity, relative file and line location
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Redact secret-bearing literals and default to locations with minimal context; make fuller excerpts an explicit review option. This narrows data in a required diagnostic return.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain actionable locations and sufficient sanitized context for manual verification

potential_excess.data_scope: Repeated reads and analysis of the same skill source
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Additional local audit and trust-calculator subprocesses; no additional remote recipient is shown
potential_excess.condition: inspect.sh performs three audits and two trust calculations in text mode, or two audits in JSON mode. benchmark.sh also audits each skill separately before scoring invokes another audit.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Inspection and benchmarking require audit results and scores, but do not explicitly require recomputing unchanged inputs.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Produce one consistent audit result, trust score and recommendation or benchmark row
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Reuse the audit result in scoring and reuse the calculated score for inspection recommendations. These are redundant actions, rather than extra fields in a necessary request.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Reuse only within an unchanged input snapshot; preserve verdict, scoring rules, error handling and output formats

potential_excess.data_scope: WEATHER_API_KEY, openai:default profile value and SSH private-key contents
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: webhook.site/abc123 for the basic fixture; evil.com/exfil for the obfuscated fixture; evil.com/collect for the time-triggered fixture
potential_excess.condition: Only independent execution of the malicious fixtures, including the scheduler's time condition; test.sh does not execute these paths
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The package declares these files to be static detection fixtures. Testing source-pattern detection requires neither real credentials nor live disclosure.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Preserve scanner-visible credential-access, obfuscation, network and time-trigger patterns
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Refuse direct execution before sensitive statements while retaining inert detection patterns; use synthetic secrets and mock transport for any deliberate execution tests. The live reads and uploads are removable actions.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep existing detection assertions effective and retain the fixtures' intended malicious signatures

potential_excess.data_scope: SSH private-key and AWS credential-file contents assigned to unused variables
potential_excess.condition: Only direct fixture execution; no remote disclosure is shown
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Static sensitive-path detection does not require live reads; the displayed account count also does not use either credential value.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Exercise sensitive-path detection and, if intentionally demonstrated, return a synthetic account-count result
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Guard against direct execution or replace live inputs with synthetic files while retaining inert detection signatures. These credential reads are redundant actions.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Maintain sensitive-fs test coverage without opening real credential files

potential_excess.data_scope: Sensitive-file link targets and full SSH private-key contents
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Persistent /tmp/project-users and /tmp/project-key symlinks; private-key contents on the direct caller's standard output
potential_excess.condition: Only direct execution of the symlink fixture, with successful link creation
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Testing symlink-attack detection requires recognizable source patterns, not real links to sensitive files or a private-key return.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Preserve detection of sensitive symlink targets
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Block direct execution or use isolated synthetic targets with cleanup. Remove the live key read and return; retaining a symlink stores a reference, not a copy of the key.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep the symlink-attack assertion effective and distinguish synthetic execution tests from static fixtures

unknowns: The installed clawhub implementation is not supplied. Its external endpoints, transmitted fields beyond the provided arguments, authentication, caches, telemetry and server retention/deletion remain unresolved (inspect.sh:38-54).
Downloaded fixture payloads are unavailable. Their subsequent reads, disclosures, persistence and deletion cannot be determined if independently executed (tests/malicious-download-exec/run.sh:2-3).

backdoor.sh is not supplied; its contents and whether the fixture copy can succeed are unknown. The setup script itself does not execute the copied file (tests/malicious-privilege-escalation/setup.sh:2-3).

Runtime input contents, filesystem permissions and caller handling of stdout are unspecified. Ordinary returns are not evidence of external disclosure; report/trend access controls and retention outside the implemented pruning are unresolved.

Fixture exclusion from distribution is claimed, but .clawignore is absent from the supplied inventory and fixture files are included. Publication filtering cannot be verified (TEST-FIXTURES-WARNING.md:30-32; CHANGELOG.md:7-11).
